Thursday, November 26, 2026

The Guarantee, the Hike, and the Handover

The war in Ukraine and the security guarantee designed to end it, the Federal Reserve's December meeting after October inflation rose again, and Houston and Texas in the weeks between an election that flipped the state and the January days when power actually changes hands.

On each board, the loud event has already happened, and the real decision sits somewhere quieter, later, and harder to move. The guarantee Kyiv is being asked to trade land for cannot be delivered by the men offering it.

The December hike is priced as settled, but the vote has not been taken and the data that could change it lands the day after. The Texas sweep is final on paper and powerless until January, while the outgoing government's court filings, contracts, and queue decisions are being made now.

Four numbers, one argument

The events were loud. These are the numbers that say who holds the leverage.

20%War-risk premium, upper-end Black Sea quotes
Insurance for CPC terminal voyages clusters at 7.5 to 10 percent of hull value, with upper quotes at 20 percent, against a third of one percent before the invasion.
€45BEuropean Commission loan proposed for Ukraine, 2027
Up to 25 billion euros military and 20 billion budget support, repayable only once Russia pays reparations, covering two-thirds of Ukraine's 2027 financing gap.
3.3%Core PCE inflation, year to October
Up from 3.1 percent in September, in the last inflation report the Fed gets before it votes on December 9. The target is 2 percent.
19 / 12Texas Senate, Republicans against Democrats
Democrats won every statewide office and flipped the House on November 3. The Senate did not move, and it confirms the regulators the new governor needs.

THE BOARD

Why The Board exists.

I don’t have a ton of time. It’s hard to keep up.

There are so many conflicting narratives, fed by conflicting interests. It feels hard to know what is true, and I know I’m not alone in that.

I often have questions I want answered, or things I don’t understand, that the news simply doesn’t cover. Not all of the time, but sometimes. When that happens, there is nowhere obvious to go for a straight answer.

In my ideal world, I build something useful to me. Something I enjoy reading. Because if I do, so will other people, and it will help them too.

The Board is a personal project. Everything here reflects my own views and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or representative of my employer.
